extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, historians, archivists, and USPTO data users
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and parsing the fields and structure from an alphabetical index of patents issued (US Patent Office annual list for 1878). The page lists patentees, invention titles, dates, monthly volume numbers, Official Gazette references, patent numbers, and cross-reference notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No.
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent number column (labelled 'No.') listing the issued patent or reissue numbers (e.g., 199, 200, 201 ... and reissue numbers shown in some places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric patent identifiers recorded in the index; may include reissue patents. Use as primary unique identifier for each entry when present. Appears in numeric form adjacent to each entry or as a separate column header 'No.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, residence, and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Main entry text including the patentee's name, residence (city, state, sometimes country), and a brief invention title or description (heading printed as 'Name, residence, and invention.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries frequently include additional assignment or co-inventor notes (e.g., 'assignor to ...', 'assignor of one-half interest to ...'), parenthetical cross-references (e.g., '(See X, assignor.)'), and flags like '(Reissue.)'. The invention title is typically a short noun or noun-phrase (e.g., 'Telephone', 'Velocipede', 'Car-coupling'). Preserve assignor and reissue annotations when parsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue (or other relevant) date for the patent as printed under the column heading 'Date.' (format: month day, year; e.g., 'Apr. 23, 1878').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are presented in abbreviated month form and occasionally repeated for grouped entries; treat as the official date associated with the index entry (usually issue date). Some entries show multiple dates in nearby text — capture the date that aligns with the specific entry row.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric code under the column heading 'Monthly volume.' corresponding to the monthly volume number in which the patent appears (e.g., 298, 793, 1100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the USPTO monthly volume reference for the patent; record as given. Values are integers and sometimes printed in groups for multiple entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference number under the heading 'Official Gazette.' indicating the Gazette page/issue reference where the patent notice appears (e.g., 87, 793, 328).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the printed Official Gazette reference exactly. These are used as bibliographic pointers to the Gazette publication and may be numeric page/issue identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment / cross-reference and reissue notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical notes and inline phrases indicating assignment relationships, co-assignors, 'See ...' cross-references, and '(Reissue.)' flags that modify the main entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These annotations describe legal/administrative aspects of the patent: assignor information (who assigned rights to whom), references to other entries or earlier listings ('See X, assignor.'), and reissue status. Retain these exactly; they are essential metadata for provenance and legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alphabetical ordering / index structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The page is an alphabetical list of patentees (heading: 'Alphabetical list of patentees for the year 1878—Continued.') with columns for the standard fields; entries are grouped and continued across pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the alphabetical ordering when reconstructing the index. Be aware entries may span lines, include line-break artifacts, and have overlapping/continued-page markers; reassemble multi-line entries into coherent records. Column alignment can be irregular in OCR/extraction — use headings to map fields.
